title: Artin's affine support estimate for the direct image at finite coefficients
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring whose additive exponent is invertible in $k$. Use the ordinary derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine morphism of finite type [pqf-def-affine-morphism] between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $Rf_*$ be the right derived functor of the module direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] on $D^+(-_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. Let $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ have constructible cohomology sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and satisfy the support condition: for every $i$ the closed support of a sheaf (the complement of the largest Zariski open on which it vanishes; by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] this is the closure of the set of points with a nonzero geometric stalk) of $\mathcal H^{-i}L$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] has dimension at most $i$, the empty set having dimension $-\infty$, as in [def-per-support-condition] read at finite coefficients. Then $Rf_*L$ is bounded with constructible cohomology sheaves and satisfies the support condition.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.1 (Artin's estimate: Rf_* of an affine morphism preserves pD^{<=0})

proof.text: Put $F_i=\mathcal H^{-i}L$. If $i<0$, its closed support has negative dimension and is therefore empty: any nonempty space has a chain consisting of one nonempty irreducible closed subset and has dimension at least zero. Thus every geometric stalk of $F_i$ is zero and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to the underlying abelian sheaf, gives $F_i=0$. Since $L$ is bounded below [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], choose $N\ge0$ such that $\mathcal H^rL=0$ for $r<-N$. The only possibly nonzero cohomology sheaves are the constructible $F_i$ for $0\le i\le N$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and their closed supports $Z_i$ have dimension at most $i$. In particular $L\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$. The zero complex is covered by taking $N=0$.

source.place: 2.1.2 and 4.1.1: support condition and reduction to the finitely many cohomology sheaves

proof.text: The positive additive exponent $e$ of the finite ring $\Lambda$ annihilates $\Lambda$ and is invertible in $k$, exactly the coefficient hypothesis of [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility]. Apply that theorem both to $L$ and to every degree-zero sheaf $F_i$: $Rf_*L$ and $Rf_*F_i$ are bounded constructible. In particular $G_{i,q}:=R^qf_*F_i$ is constructible for every $q$. Since a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field), [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes $X,Y$ Noetherian. They are quasi-compact and quasi-separated: quasi-compactness is part of finite type, and separatedness is assumed. These are the hypotheses needed below for constructible supports and finite irreducible decompositions.

source.place: 4.1.1 and its bounded constructible setting; finite-type constructibility is the existing theorem thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility

proof.text: Fix $0\le i\le N$. Write $S(F_i)$ for the set of points with a nonzero geometric stalk, as in [def-kun-support]. If $x\in S(F_i)$, then $x\in Z_i$ and the irreducible closed subset $\overline{\{x\}}$ is contained in $Z_i$. Its generic point is $x$, so [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(x)=\dim\overline{\{x\}}\le\dim Z_i\le i$. Consequently $S(F_i)\subset E_i(X)$. The underlying abelian sheaf of $F_i$ is torsion: multiplication by the positive integer $e$ of Step 2 kills every section, because it kills $1\in\Lambda$.

source.place: Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I: translate the closed-support bound into the E_i support hypothesis

proof.text: For $q\ge0$, [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of $G_{i,q}$ with the abelian higher direct image $R^qf_*(F_i)_{\mathrm{ab}}$. Apply [lem-kun-affine-direct-image-support-bound] with $K=k$, $a=i$ and the torsion abelian sheaf $(F_i)_{\mathrm{ab}}$. Both schemes are finite type over $k$, $f$ is affine, $i\ge0$, and Step 3 verifies precisely the required stalk-support containment. It follows that $S(G_{i,q})\subset E_{i-q}(Y)$. In particular every point $y$ with nonzero geometric stalk has $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(y)\le i-q$. If $i-q<0$, this set is empty by the convention in the cited estimate.

source.place: Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I; coefficient comparison supplied by the existing higher-direct-image comparison node

proof.text: Put $S=S(G_{i,q})$ and $Z=\overline S$. This $Z$ is the closed support in the statement: on an open $U$ disjoint from $S$, all geometric stalks of $G_{i,q}|_U$ vanish, hence the restriction vanishes by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]; conversely a zero restriction has zero stalks. By [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-support-constructible], $S$ is constructible (the coefficient ring is finite, the sheaf constructible by Step 2, and $Y$ qcqs). By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], write $Z=C_1\cup\cdots\cup C_r$ for its finitely many distinct irreducible components. Each $C_j$ has a generic point $\eta_j$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. When $Z$ is empty there are no components.

source.place: Tag 09YS, lemma-support-constructible (3); closed support and irreducible components

proof.text: Every $\eta_j$ of Step 5 belongs to $S$. Here are the elementary topological details, rather than an appeal to another proof. Remove all components other than $C_j$: the open $V=Y\setminus\bigcup_{h\ne j}C_h$ meets $C_j$ in a nonempty open, and $S\cap V$ is dense there since $\overline S=Z$. Therefore $S\cap C_j$ is dense in $C_j$. By [def-weil-constructible-subset], write $S$ as a finite union of locally closed subsets. Their intersections with $C_j$ are locally closed and their closures cover $C_j$; irreducibility forces one of these closures to equal $C_j$. That intersection, being locally closed and dense, is a nonempty open of $C_j$, and so contains its generic point $\eta_j$. Hence $\eta_j\in S$. This argument proves exactly the generic-point fact needed here from the finite-union definition; it does not assume that a constructible sheaf has closed stalk support.

source.place: Tag 005K, lemma-generic-point-in-constructible, elementary finite-union argument written out

proof.text: For every component $C_j$ of $Z$, Steps 4 and 6 and [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] give $\dim C_j=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\eta_j)\le i-q$. Thus $\dim Z\le i-q$. Indeed any chain of irreducible closed subsets of a finite union of closed subsets lies in one member: its largest irreducible subset lies in one member by irreducibility, and then so does the whole chain. Hence the dimension of a finite union is the maximum of their dimensions. For $i-q<0$, Step 4 instead gives $S=\varnothing$, so $Z=\varnothing$ and $G_{i,q}=0$ by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. We have proved the closed-support bound for every $R^qf_*F_i$, including the vanishing when $q>i$.

source.place: Tag 0B1C in Tag 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic (6); combined with Tag 0F0X via Step 4

proof.text: The derived direct image commutes with shifts and carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated], applied to the additive left exact module direct image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For $m\in\mathbf Z$ put $q=i-m$. Then $\mathcal H^{-m}(Rf_*(F_i[i]))=R^qf_*F_i$. If $q\ge0$, Step 7 bounds its closed-support dimension by $i-q=m$. If $q<0$, this sheaf vanishes: compute the right derived functor on an injective resolution $F_i\to I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$ as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; the direct-image complex has zero terms in negative degrees. Therefore every $Rf_*(F_i[i])$ satisfies the required support condition.

source.place: 4.1.1, cohomology-sheaf reduction; exactness and shifts of the derived direct image

proof.text: The support condition is closed under extensions. For a distinguished triangle $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$, the long exact cohomology sequence of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] gives an exact segment $\mathcal H^{-m}A\to\mathcal H^{-m}B\to\mathcal H^{-m}C$. On the open complement of the union of the two outer closed supports the outer sheaves vanish, so exactness forces the middle sheaf to vanish. Its closed support is contained in that finite union, whose dimension is at most $m$ when both outer objects satisfy the condition (the finite-union dimension argument was written in Step 7). This proves extension closure directly, for all integers $m$.

source.place: 1.3.3-1.3.6 and 4.1.1: extension closure from the cohomological functor

proof.text: Use the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] and the truncation triangles [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. Since Step 1 gives cohomology only in $[-N,0]$, the successive standard truncations have triangles $\tau^{\le r-1}L\to\tau^{\le r}L\to(\mathcal H^rL)[-r]\to(\tau^{\le r-1}L)[1]$ for $-N\le r\le0$. Their bottom object $\tau^{\le-N-1}L$ is zero (all its cohomology is zero), and their top object $\tau^{\le0}L$ is $L$. The third objects are exactly the $F_i[i]$ with $i=-r$. Apply $Rf_*$, using its triangulated property from Step 8. Starting at zero, Step 8 supplies the support condition on every third object and Step 9 supplies the induction step. After the finitely many values of $r$, $Rf_*L$ satisfies the support condition. Its boundedness and constructible cohomology were already established in Step 2. No finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis on $L$ or separable-closure hypothesis on $k$ has been used.

source.place: 4.1.1, reduction to H^r(L)[-r], with the standard truncation construction of 1.3.2(i)

proof_origin.place: Theorem 4.1.1, ordinary cohomology-sheaf reduction; the sheaf estimate is Stacks Tag 0F0X, and the closed-support conversion is written out from constructibility and finite irreducible decomposition.

Step 3 shows S(F_i) is in E_i via the trdeg node, and the underlying sheaf is torsion. Step 4 uses the sheaf-level forget comparison plus 0F0X to get E_{i-q}. Step 7 bounds dim Z by the maximum over components, and the sheaf is 0 when i-q<0. Step 8 checks the shift H^{-m}(Rf_*(F_i[i])) = R^{i-m}f_*F_i, which vanishes for q<0. Step 9 proves extension closure from the long exact sequence. Step 10 is the finite truncation induction from tau^{<=-N-1}L=0 up to L. Edge cases checked: L=0, Lambda=0, q>i, f=id, lisse sheaf on a curve. The 11 tool_uses are all generic inputs and accepted.
